articles.headline: Private Equity Fund Managers Commit More Personal Capital to New Funds
articles.summary: Indian private equity and venture capital managers are increasing their own capital commitments to new funds to signal confidence to investors. Firms like Motilal Oswal and Carnelian are committing 10-12% and over ₹100 crore respectively, far exceeding the regulatory minimum of 2.5%. The move comes as fundraising becomes concentrated in fewer, larger vehicles amid delayed return concerns.

articles.headline: CCPA Fines Luxury Hotel for Mandatory Restaurant Service Charge Collection
articles.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) fined New Delhi’s Shangri-La Eros ₹1 lakh for adding a 10% service charge to bills. The regulator ruled that automatically adding the fee and requiring customers to 'opt-out' pressures consumers and violates guidelines. The 2022 rules state restaurants cannot force service charges or levy GST on them, a stance upheld by the Delhi high court.

articles.headline: India Records Rising Winter Temperatures and Increased Thermal Volatility
articles.summary: Analysis of India Meteorological Department data reveals winter temperatures have risen by 0.07°C per decade since 1901. Warmer winters are becoming more frequent, driven by El Niño and broader climate change. The shift impacts water availability, cropping patterns, and rural incomes, while rising night-time temperatures during seasonal transitions are disrupting sleep patterns.

articles.headline: Study Shows High Prevalence of Zombie Firms Weighing on Indian Economy
articles.summary: A Dun and Bradstreet study indicates that while the share of 'zombie' firms (companies unable to cover interest payments for three years) has dropped to 14.2%, they still pose risks. India leads many Asian peers in zombie firm prevalence by assets. These firms often survive through bank 'evergreening,' generating negative returns on assets while depressing overall GDP growth and inflation.

articles.headline: Indian IT Services Firms Launch Policing Software for AI Agents
articles.summary: Top Indian IT firms, including TCS, HCLTech, and Tech Mahindra, are developing software to govern and police autonomous AI agents. The move addresses corporate fears that digital workers could access unauthorized data or 'go rogue.' Global firms are seeking 'agentic control planes' to manage AI performance, costs, and security as agentic AI moves beyond isolated deployments.

articles.headline: Private Banks Lag Public Lenders in Financial Inclusion Credit Schemes
articles.summary: Private sector banks are trailing public lenders in implementing government schemes like PM Mudra, PM SVANidhi, and PM Vishwakarma. For street vendor credit, public banks sanctioned 74% of applications compared to 20% for private banks. Structural gaps and high interest-subvention claim backlogs at lenders like HDFC and Axis Bank are hampering delivery to small entrepreneurs and artisans.

articles.headline: Centre Proposes ₹1,150 Crore Aid for NCR Industries to Curb Pollution
articles.summary: The Centre is considering a ₹1,150 crore scheme to provide one-time capital support for roughly 600 industrial units in the National Capital Region. The funds will help units in textile and food sectors retrofit plants with air pollution control devices and effluent treatment systems. The move aims to improve air quality ahead of the winter smog season in the Delhi-NCR region.

articles.headline: Indian Refiners Pivot to Gulf Oil as Russian Freight Costs Surge
articles.summary: Indian refiners are increasing purchases of Persian Gulf crude as rising freight costs make long-haul Russian shipments less economical. Some Iraqi cargoes are being sold at deep discounts to offset high shipping rates. While Russia remains India's top supplier, state-owned refiners like BPCL and HPCL report that the lack of commercial viability is reducing Russian oil imports.

articles.headline: India and US Fine-Tuning Proposed Trade Deal for Finalization
articles.summary: Union Minister Piyush Goyal announced that India and the US have concluded most discussions on a proposed trade agreement and are currently fine-tuning the deal. Bilateral trade reached $140.76 billion in FY26. Goyal emphasized that India's expanding network of trade agreements will provide preferential access to economies accounting for 76% of global GDP.

articles.headline: Oil Prices Ease Globally on Hopes of Gulf Conflict De-escalation
articles.summary: Global oil prices fell after surging to near six-month highs last week. Brent crude futures dropped 1.28% to $115.23, while US WTI fell 1.7% to $101.51. The decline is driven by hopes of easing hostilities between the US and Iran, though investors remain cautious due to persistent attacks on Saudi Arabian production infrastructure.

articles.headline: Defence Council Clears $22 Billion Military Equipment Procurement Proposals
articles.summary: India’s Defence Acquisition Council has granted in-principle approval for arms and equipment deals worth ₹2.12 trillion ($22.27 billion). The approvals include the procurement of very short-range air defence systems, counter-drone technology, surveillance and strike systems, and long-range kamikaze drones to bolster national security.

articles.headline: Centre Extends Export Risk Cover Support Until March 2027
articles.summary: The Department of Commerce has extended a scheme providing risk coverage to exporters facing high shipping and insurance costs due to West Asian geopolitical disruptions. The scheme, now valid until 31 March 2027, offers up to 95% risk cover to protect Indian exporters against premium hikes and shipping uncertainties.

articles.headline: L Catterton Invests in AI-Powered Shopping Platform Glance
articles.summary: US-based investment firm L Catterton has made a strategic investment in Glance, an AI-driven personal shopping platform owned by InMobi. Glance uses agentic AI to provide hyper-personalized product discovery on smartphone lock screens and connected TVs. The capital infusion will support Glance's global expansion, particularly in the US market.

articles.headline: AI Giant Anthropic Files for Landmark Initial Public Offering
articles.summary: Anthropic has filed for an IPO that could be the largest ever, potentially surpassing SpaceX's $86 billion record. While the company reported a net loss of $13 billion in H1 2026 on revenues of $80.7 billion, its valuation could reach $1.5 trillion. The filing comes despite CEO Dario Amodei's warnings about existential risks from advanced AI models.

articles.headline: Verizon and AWS Sign $2 Billion AI Infrastructure Agreement
articles.summary: Verizon has signed an AI infrastructure deal worth over $2 billion with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to enhance its technology capabilities. The telecom major also raised its annual wireless subscriber forecast following strong Q3 demand for simplified plans. Verizon reported 406,000 monthly-bill paying wireless subscriber additions, nearly double analyst estimates.

articles.headline: Indian Brands Adopt Generative AI for Festive Marketing Campaigns
articles.summary: Advertisers in India are increasingly using AI to create festive season campaign assets, reducing production costs by up to 80%. Brands like Oppo and SBI Life are using AI for script ideation and video production. Festive advertising accounts for roughly ₹21,000 crore of annual spend, and AI is helping companies deploy a larger volume of personalized creatives.

articles.headline: Sembcorp Green Infra Targets $394 Million via India IPO
articles.summary: Sembcorp Industries is meeting investors for a proposed $394 million IPO of its Indian unit, Sembcorp Green Infra. The renewable energy firm, backed by Temasek, could launch the offering as early as December. India's IPO market is currently seeing record momentum, with nearly $18 billion raised this year, challenging previous annual records.

articles.headline: Kotak Mahindra Bank NIM Sharply Declines Due to FCNR Deposit Costs
articles.summary: Kotak Mahindra Bank’s net interest margin (NIM) fell 22 basis points to 4.31% in Q2, primarily due to interest outgo on FCNR(B) deposits. While the bank's loan book grew 19% to ₹5.5 trillion, its return on equity (RoE) of 11.6% continues to trail peers like ICICI and HDFC. Management indicated credit costs could rise by 12-15 bps once ECL norms take effect.

articles.headline: Tata Motors CV Profits Pressured by Rising Steel and Rubber Costs
articles.summary: Tata Motors' standalone revenue grew 42% in Q2 to ₹23,930 crore, supported by strong commercial vehicle volumes. However, Ebitda margins fell to 11.4% as surging steel and rubber prices impacted profitability. Management warned that a further commodity cost increase of 150-200 bps is expected in Q3, making future margin protection dependent on price hikes.

articles.headline: Incoming HDFC Bank CEO Faces Leadership Continuity and Reputation Challenges
articles.summary: Anup Bagchi takes charge as HDFC Bank CEO on 27 October amidst concerns over senior management departures and governance controversies. Bagchi must navigate a narrowed valuation premium and slowing retail lending growth. The bank's CASA ratio slipped to 31.6% in the September quarter, and FII shareholding dropped to 39%, reflecting institutional concerns post-merger.

articles.headline: Sebi Relaxes Margin Rules to Facilitate Same-Day Share Trading
articles.summary: Market regulator Sebi has eased margin requirements for investors using sale proceeds to buy new stocks on the same day via the early pay-in mechanism. Effective February 2027, the move reduces the upfront funding burden for brokers. The change aims to boost cash market participation, which saw a 7% turnover decline on the NSE in the previous fiscal year.

articles.headline: Hyundai India Launches Bayon SUV to Target Mid-Size Segment Growth
articles.summary: Hyundai Motor India has launched the Bayon SUV with a starting price of ₹9.99 lakh. The company aims to boost annual mid-size SUV sales to 250,000 units within 12 months. Positioned as a technology-led product with AI voice assistants, the Bayon will compete with the Maruti Grand Vitara and Tata Sierra as Hyundai seeks to regain ground in the utility vehicle market.

articles.headline: Biotech Startup PopVax Advances mRNA Vaccine to Human Clinical Trials
articles.summary: Hyderabad-based biotech PopVax has moved its fridge-stable mRNA covid-19 vaccine into Phase 1 trials in Australia. The five-year-old firm, which has raised over $30 million, is also developing first-in-class immunotherapies for liver and pancreatic cancers. CEO Soham Sankaran aims to use AI to design targeted therapeutics against viral threats within weeks.

articles.headline: Swiss Watchmakers Lean on Indian Heritage and Faith to Captivate Collectors
articles.summary: Swiss brands are launching India-exclusive watches featuring religious motifs and local languages. Jacob & Co. unveiled a ₹4.25 crore Lord Ram timepiece, while TAG Heuer launched a Carrera featuring 24 Indian languages. Swiss watch exports to India rose 28.5% in early 2026, making India the 14th largest market, aided by lower customs duties under the India-EFTA pact.

articles.headline: Indian Epic 'Ramayana' Targets Global Mainstream with English Theatrical Release
articles.summary: The big-budget Indian film 'Ramayana' is heading for an English release to attract non-diaspora international audiences. Entertainment experts say English dubbing for live-action films signals growing confidence in Indian stories. The strategy follows global success trends seen in Korean and Japanese content, aiming to move beyond traditional overseas Indian markets.

articles.headline: Israel Heads to Fateful Polls as Netanyahu Fights for Political Survival
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces a tight re-election race today, with his legacy and national security at stake. Despite initial backlash following the October 7 attacks, Netanyahu has clawed back support. Opponents argue he has failed to convert battlefield wins into diplomatic success, while his supporters credit him with devastating strikes against Hezbollah and Iran.

articles.headline: Combination Cancer Drug Trial Boosts Survival for Aggressive Lung Cancer
articles.summary: A study presented in Madrid shows that combining Amgen’s Imdelltra with AstraZeneca’s Imfinzi extended the lives of small cell lung cancer patients by eight months. The dual therapy reduced the risk of death by 58%. Oncologists described the survival benefit as an 'unprecedented step forward' for one of the world's deadliest cancers with typically poor prognoses.

articles.headline: Russian Energy Insider Sues Shadow Fleet Traders Over Oil Sale Proceeds
articles.summary: Former Deutsche Bank executive Igor Soglayev has sued the sanctioned 'Coral' network of oil traders in Dubai and Brazil. Soglayev alleges he was cheated out of $700 million in Russian energy sale proceeds. The legal battle provides a rare look at the shadow fleet operations that enable Moscow to bypass Western sanctions and sell tens of billions of dollars of oil annually.

articles.headline: Uday Kotak Warns of $160 Billion FCNR Deposit Repayment Cliff
articles.summary: Financial veteran Uday Kotak has urged policymakers to prepare for a $160 billion 'repayment cliff' for FCNR(B) deposits due in three to five years. Speaking in Mumbai, he also flagged risks from the excessive financialization of gold, which has led to a surge in imports and is putting pressure on India's external economic balance and financial structure.

articles.headline: Indian Rupee Settles 22 Paise Lower at 95.15 Against Dollar
articles.summary: The Indian rupee hit a new low, depreciating 22 paise to settle at 95.15 against the US dollar. Elevated crude oil prices and ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East weighed on the currency. While local stock market recovery provided some cushion, rising US Treasury yields and broad dollar strength continues to pressure the rupee's external value.

articles.headline: Saudi Aramco Negotiates $10 Billion Loan with Consortium of Global Banks
articles.summary: State-backed Saudi Aramco is nearing a $10 billion revolving credit facility deal with banks including Citi, HSBC, and JPMorgan. The financing comes as Middle East conflicts threaten oil infrastructure. The facility is expected to be priced at 60 basis points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate. Other Gulf energy firms, including QatarEnergy, have also tapped debt markets recently.

articles.headline: ITC Hotels Reports 51.4% Rise in Second Quarter Net Profit
articles.summary: ITC Hotels posted a consolidated net profit of ₹201 crore for Q2, driven by a 17.4% rise in room revenue. Total revenue from operations increased to ₹1,054 crore. The company expects strong performance in the second half of the fiscal year, supported by seasonally higher demand for weddings, sporting events, and corporate exhibitions.

articles.headline: PTC India Board Approves Proposal for Subsidiary-Led Mineral Exchange
articles.summary: PTC India has cleared a proposal to set up a wholly-owned subsidiary to operate a mineral exchange in India. The company will invest up to ₹65 crore in the venture. The exchange will facilitate delivery-based electronic trading of permitted minerals. The move aims to bring organized trading mechanisms to the mineral sector under applicable government rules.

articles.headline: EY Challenges Tax Ruling on Payments for Deputed Staff in India
articles.summary: Global consulting firm EY has moved the Supreme Court against a Delhi High Court ruling regarding tax on seconded employees. The high court treated payments made by Indian entities to EY US as taxable 'fees for technical services' rather than simple salary reimbursements. The eventual ruling will affect how multinational firms structure global capability centres and withholding tax.

articles.headline: India Pushes for Oil Palm Expansion via ₹11,040 Crore National Mission
articles.summary: India's National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm aims to produce 25.45 million tonnes of edible oil by 2030-31 to reduce a $18.3 billion import bill. The program has expanded oil palm cultivation to 300,000 hectares across 15 states. Private players like Godrej Agrovet and Patanjali are investing in integrated mills, though the crop requires a long four-year gestation period.

articles.headline: Rising Airfares Force Indian Travellers to Cancel Year-End Holiday Plans
articles.summary: Domestic airfares in India have surged 30-40% year-on-year, driven by high fuel costs and a weaker rupee. Return flights to popular destinations like Goa and Port Blair have seen sharp spikes, forcing travellers to switch to trains or cheaper local destinations. Airlines have reduced flight frequencies on several routes to manage operating expenses, further limiting seat availability.

articles.headline: Modern Wellness Trends Rebrand Yoga Nidra as Scientific NSDR Protocol
articles.summary: The traditional practice of yoga nidra is being adopted in global wellness as 'Non-Sleep Deep Rest' (NSDR), a term coined by neuroscientist Andrew Huberman. While yoga nidra involves spiritual intention-setting, NSDR focuses on cognitive recovery and focus. Studies show that these practices can lower physiological arousal, although researchers caution they are not yet proven brain enhancers.

articles.headline: Fitness Experts Recommend Daily Exercises for Core Strength and Posture
articles.summary: Fitness professionals suggest that certain low-stress exercises like push-ups, dead hangs, and face pulls can be performed daily to improve foundational strength and posture. These movements help develop body control and counteract the physical strain of desk jobs. Controlled movements, rather than heavy weights, are emphasized for daily maintenance of shoulder and spine health.

articles.headline: Indian Wellness Retreats Incorporate Farm Animals for Stress Management
articles.summary: Wellness resorts in Pune, Udupi, and Haryana are adding cow-petting and equine interactions to their treatments. Properties like Swastik and Fazlani offer 'gau sparsh chikitsa' and horse grooming to help guests reduce cortisol levels and switch off mentally. Psychologists note that non-judgmental social interaction with animals can shift attention away from repetitive stressful thoughts.

articles.headline: Government Reassesses LTCG Tax and STT Following Investor Feedback
articles.summary: The Indian government has initiated a reassessment of Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax and Securities Transaction Tax (STT). Officials have sought views from investors and tax experts to potentially relax these levies. The move aims to support domestic markets and attract foreign capital following a significant exit by overseas investors, with LTCG mop-up reaching ₹1.29 lakh crore in FY25.

articles.headline: Petroleum Export Earnings Surge 50% Despite Lower Shipment Volumes
articles.summary: India's petroleum product export earnings grew 50% year-on-year to ₹2.59 lakh crore in the first half of FY27. While shipment volumes declined by 16%, high international fuel prices and a sharply weaker rupee significantly boosted rupee-term returns. Diesel remains the top contributor, with export earnings increasing 58% despite a 19% volume dip due to high domestic demand.

articles.headline: Dailyhunt Parent VerSe Innovation Valuation Slashed by 90% by UK Investor
articles.summary: British investment firm Baillie Gifford has marked down the fair value of Dailyhunt's parent company, VerSe Innovation, to approximately $576 million. This represents a 90% drop from its 2022 peak valuation of $5 billion. The markdown follows operational pressures and a decline in revenue for the 2025-26 fiscal year, partly due to regulatory bans on real-money gaming advertisements.

articles.headline: Data Protection Board of India Remains Non-Functional Despite Looming Deadlines
articles.summary: RTI responses show the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) has recorded zero expenditure on salaries or office setup despite a ₹10 crore budget. With framework registration for consent managers scheduled for November 13, the lack of appointments and infrastructure threatens to stall the implementation of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

articles.headline: CERT-In Coordinates Urgent Patching of PHP Vulnerabilities in Government Portals
articles.summary: India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In is working with state authorities to patch critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language used by thousands of government websites. Priority is being given to health and banking portals that store large amounts of citizen data. While major national digital infrastructure is unaffected, many district and municipal portals remain at risk.

articles.headline: Microsoft India Offers Voluntary Exit Packages Amid Global AI Pivot
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced a time-bound voluntary exit offer for eligible employees in India and other global hubs. The program, available to staff at level 70 and below, provides one month of base salary per year of service, health insurance, and career support. The move comes as Microsoft shifts its investment focus toward cloud and AI infrastructure, including a $20.5 billion plan for India.

articles.headline: SpaceX Secures 40 Billion Dollar AI Chip Financing Deal with Apollo
articles.summary: An affiliate of Apollo Global Management will purchase Nvidia AI chips and server hardware to lease back to SpaceX in a deal worth $40 billion. The transaction uses a special purpose vehicle to keep liabilities off SpaceX’s balance sheet. The funding is intended to support Elon Musk's goals for Moon and Mars missions by providing massive computing power for AI development.

articles.headline: Rupee Plunges to 95.18 on Oil Prices and Fading IPO Inflows
articles.summary: The Indian rupee fell below the 95/$ mark on Monday, closing at a near two-week low of 95.18. The decline was driven by elevated global oil prices and the fading of dollar inflows related to the Jio Platforms IPO. Importer dollar demand remained strong despite the RBI's recent 'midnight measures' intended to cap excess depreciation and manage spot market liquidity.

articles.headline: India’s Strategic Mining Sector Faces Severe Execution and Regulatory Bottlenecks
articles.summary: Despite global concerns over critical mineral supplies, India has only operationalised 125 out of 733 auctioned mineral blocks. A government review identified land acquisition as the primary hurdle, alongside fragmented records and overlapping state levies. The Centre has urged states to adopt a 'mission mode' coordination framework to bolster energy security and local extraction.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to Hear Bike Taxi Aggregator Appeals After November 16
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has scheduled a hearing for late November on the legality of bike taxi operations in Karnataka. The state government has challenged a High Court ruling that allowed the services, citing passenger safety and insurance concerns. While the Centre has reportedly supported the operations, the Karnataka government maintains a ban on non-electric bike taxis.

articles.headline: Unified Tax Framework Proposed for Textiles to Enhance Global Competitiveness
articles.summary: The Centre is developing an integrated tax framework for the textile sector, covering GST, customs duties, and anti-dumping measures. The proposal aims to provide duty relief on raw materials and imported machinery. Industry players have sought a six-month waiver on polyester products to compete with rivals from China, Bangladesh, and Vietnam in man-made fibre exports.

articles.headline: Banks Retreat from Forex Swap Deals Following RBI Scrutiny
articles.summary: Large banks have pulled back from buy-sell foreign exchange swap deals after the RBI expressed concerns over the transactions. Lenders had been using excess rupee liquidity to buy dollars and invest in US Treasury bills to earn returns near 9%. The regulator reportedly wants banks to use the liquidity for domestic lending instead of placing dollars abroad for short-term gains.

articles.headline: Jakson Group to Invest 6,863 Crore in Integrated Solar Plant
articles.summary: Jakson Group plans to establish a solar manufacturing facility in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, with an investment of ₹6,863 crore. The plant will produce 10 GW of silicon ingots/wafers and 5 GW of solar cells. The project will be developed in phases, with the first phase expected to begin commercial production by May 2028, potentially creating 2,000 jobs in the clean energy sector.

articles.headline: NBFCs Curb Rural Lending in Drought-Hit Regions to Manage Stress
articles.summary: Major non-bank lenders, including Shriram Finance and M&M Financial, are moderating fresh loans in drought-affected parts of Karnataka and Central India. A 13% monsoon deficit has raised concerns over rural repayment capacity. Lenders are tightening loan-to-value ratios and strengthening collection mechanisms to manage potential asset quality stress in the agriculture-dependent economy.

articles.headline: Hyundai Motor India Bets on Mass-Market SUVs to Gain Market Share
articles.summary: Hyundai plans to launch two mass-market SUVs, including an electric model, to regain share in India's competitive mid-size SUV segment. The company aims for annual volumes of over 250,000 units from the Creta and the newly launched Bayon. Hyundai expects SUVs to drive 75% of its total domestic sales by FY28, up from the current 69% contribution.

articles.headline: Pharmaceutical Giants Invest Billions in AI-Led Drug Discovery Alliances
articles.summary: Top drugmakers including Novo Nordisk, Sanofi, and AstraZeneca are investing billions in AI to compress drug development timelines. While traditional trials take a decade, AI tools are already cutting early-stage design time by up to 50%. However, experts note that while discovery is faster, clinical trial phases remain a significant bottleneck that still requires years of testing.

articles.headline: Anthropic flags 'existential risks' in long-awaited IPO filing
articles.summary: AI startup Anthropic has filed for an IPO, warning that its technology carries existential risks to humanity. The company reported an $80.7 billion net loss on $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026. The debut comes amid high scrutiny over AI safety and competition with OpenAI, with the listing expected as early as the week of November 9.

articles.headline: Tata Consumer sees all-round growth; profit rises 16% in Q2
articles.summary: Tata Consumer Products reported a 16% increase in consolidated net profit to ₹469.30 crore for the second quarter. Revenue grew 13% to ₹3,666.13 crore, driven by strong performance in the India-branded business, particularly in packaged foods and premium salt. However, operating margins narrowed slightly due to higher raw material costs and domestic investment.

articles.headline: Microsoft to offer buyouts to 60,000 workers in latest cost cut
articles.summary: Microsoft Corp plans to offer voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 employees as part of efforts to streamline operations and reallocate resources toward AI. The move affects less than 30% of its workforce. Eligible staff will receive benefits similar to standard severance packages. This follows a trend of tech giants trimming headcount despite record profits.

articles.headline: Hyundai India tasks Bayon with meeting Creta's target
articles.summary: Hyundai Motor India has launched the Bayon SUV, priced between ₹10.18 lakh and ₹18 lakh, to compete in the mid-size segment. The company hopes the new model will replicate the sales success of its Creta model. Despite a 3.2% decline in domestic sales in the April-September period, Hyundai is targeting aggressive growth with its expanded SUV portfolio.

articles.headline: Nazara Technologies reports Q2 profit of ₹35.36 crore
articles.summary: Gaming firm Nazara Technologies posted a net profit of ₹35.36 crore for the September quarter, driven by strong growth in its gaming segment. Revenue from operations reached a record ₹803 crore, up 53% year-on-year. The company credited the success to its 'Publishing 2.0' strategy and the performance of recent acquisitions like Comic Con India and Fusebox.

articles.headline: ITC Hotels sees Q2 profit jumping 52% to ₹202 crore
articles.summary: ITC Hotels reported a 52% year-on-year jump in net profit to ₹202.65 crore for the second quarter. Revenue grew 22% to ₹1,047.72 crore, supported by healthy demand across all segments including business travel and MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions). Occupancy rates remained high at 81% with a 14% growth in average daily rates.

articles.headline: Akasa Air raises ₹450 crore from share sale to existing investors
articles.summary: Akasa Air has raised ₹450 crore through a rights issue to existing investors, including the Jhunjhunwala family. The funds will be used for expansion plans and meeting operating expenses. This is the airline's second fundraise in 2026. The carrier is focusing on long-term growth despite challenges like rising fuel costs and global supply chain issues.

articles.headline: TSFL board OKs 3.74% stake sale in TVS Holdings
articles.summary: TVS Sundaram Family Ltd (TSFL) has approved the sale of a 3.74% stake in TVS Holdings through a block deal or other market mechanisms. The sale, comprising over 7.55 lakh shares, is for the benefit of existing members of the promoter group. The transaction is expected to be completed by November 2, 2026.

articles.headline: Shanthi Gears Q2 PAT down 27% at ₹15.7 crore
articles.summary: Shanthi Gears, a subsidiary of Tube Investments of India, reported a 27% decline in net profit to ₹15.7 crore for the second quarter. Revenue from operations also decreased to ₹128 crore. The company cited higher depreciation and amortization costs, along with increased expenses, as reasons for the lower bottom line.

articles.headline: Almost half of domestic coal-based power plants have critically low stocks
articles.summary: Out of 176 domestic coal-based power plants in India, 85 have critically low coal stocks, defined as less than 25% of the normative requirement. This comes as electricity demand surged 23.4% in the first ten days of October. Total coal stocks at these plants fell to 17.67 million tonnes as of October 25, raising concerns about potential power supply disruptions.

articles.headline: Govt extends RELIEF scheme for exporters till March amid W. Asia crisis
articles.summary: The Commerce Ministry has extended the Remission of Expenses for Logistic Violation for Export Facilitation (RELIEF) scheme until March 31, 2027. The move aims to support exporters facing high freight costs and insurance premiums due to the West Asian crisis. The scheme provides a 95% risk cover for shipments to specified regions to ensure continuity of operations.

articles.headline: SEBI shouldn’t encourage retail activity in SME platform
articles.summary: An editorial argues against SEBI's proposal to lower entry barriers for retail investors on SME IPO platforms. It notes that SME stocks are highly speculative and illiquid, making them risky for small investors. The piece suggests that current higher thresholds protect retail investors from potential losses and that loosening these rules could lead to market instability.

articles.headline: Revenue share: Have States lost out?
articles.summary: An analysis of fiscal devolution shows that the combined revenue receipts of States as a percentage of the total have returned to levels seen during the 10th Finance Commission period. The report highlights that increased cess and surcharges by the Centre, which are not shareable with States, have reduced the actual pool available for devolution, impacting State finances.

articles.headline: Robust battery ecosystem vital for clean energy shift
articles.summary: India needs to build a self-reliant battery manufacturing ecosystem to support its 500 GW renewable energy target by 2030. The report emphasizes the need for domestic processing of minerals like lithium and graphite, as well as developing indigenous cell-making technology. Currently, India relies heavily on imports, particularly from China, for battery components.

articles.headline: RBI measures on forex management: Some implications
articles.summary: The RBI has introduced new measures to manage foreign exchange risk, including restrictions on rebooking cancelled forward contracts and lowering the threshold for reporting large transactions. While aimed at curbing volatility, experts warn these steps could increase compliance costs for banks and limit flexibility for businesses managing their currency exposure.

articles.headline: India and the US oil nexus
articles.summary: A strategic partnership is emerging between India and the US in the oil sector, with Indian refineries potentially processing Venezuelan crude for the US market. The Jamnagar refinery's capacity to handle heavy crude makes it a key player in this strategy. This move could help the US stabilize global oil prices while providing India with a steady supply of energy.

articles.headline: Brokerage profits grow in September quarter despite market slowdown
articles.summary: Indian brokerage firms reported strong year-on-year growth in the September quarter, even as cash market turnover fell 11.7% sequentially. Companies like Angel One and Motilal Oswal saw profits rise due to higher contributions from margin funding and other segments. However, a slowing primary market and regulatory changes remain key challenges for the industry.

articles.headline: Rising crude oil prices affect sentiment for small-caps
articles.summary: The Nifty small-cap 100 index fell for the fourth consecutive session, dropping 1.1% on Monday. Investors are concerned about rising crude oil prices and the impact of potential interest rate hikes on smaller companies. Analysts suggest that while long-term growth prospects remain, short-term volatility is likely as valuations are adjusted in a high-rate environment.

articles.headline: Nifty snaps four-day losing streak on pull-back rally
articles.summary: The Nifty 50 ended its four-day losing streak, gaining 153 points to close at 22,753.20. The recovery was led by the healthcare, IT, and metal sectors, which rose over 1% each. Positive global cues and a slight dip in crude oil prices supported the rally. However, market experts remain cautious as foreign institutional investors continue to sell Indian equities.

articles.headline: Markets will reward growth, not just size: Helios’ Dinshaw Irani
articles.summary: Dinshaw Irani, CEO of Helios Capital, believes that while global uncertainties exist, India's structural growth story remains intact. He suggests that mid- and small-cap companies in sectors like auto components and consumer discretionary will continue to perform well. Irani also notes that foreign investors are becoming more selective, focusing on earnings growth over company size.

articles.headline: Brazil's stock index hit lower circuit on Lula win
articles.summary: Brazil’s Bovespa index fell 10% on Monday, triggering a circuit breaker, following the presidential election victory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Investors are concerned about potential changes in economic policy under the new leftist government. The Brazilian real also weakened significantly against the US dollar as markets reacted to the political shift.

articles.headline: ICICI Pru Fund invests ₹210 cr in Raymond Realty
articles.summary: ICICI Prudential Real Estate Development Fund has invested ₹210 crore in a project by Raymond Realty in Mumbai. The investment is part of the fund's strategy to support high-quality residential developments in key urban markets. Raymond Realty plans to use the capital to accelerate the construction and delivery of its ongoing projects.

articles.headline: FCNR(B) rush squeezes margins; pvt banks feel heat
articles.summary: Private banks in India are facing pressure on net interest margins due to a surge in high-cost Foreign Currency Non-Resident (B) deposits. While these inflows have provided short-term liquidity, the interest rates offered (7.5-10%) are significantly higher than standard domestic deposits. Analysts expect this to impact bank earnings in the coming quarters.

articles.headline: Bank of Maharashtra reports 41% jump in Q2 profit
articles.summary: Bank of Maharashtra posted a 41% increase in net profit to ₹2,310 crore for the second quarter. The bank saw robust growth in both its retail and corporate lending segments. Net interest income rose 22% to ₹3,954 crore, while asset quality continued to improve with a decline in gross NPA levels. The bank's NIM stood at a healthy 3.16%.

articles.headline: Beauty, personal care segment sees strong festival growth
articles.summary: The beauty and personal care industry is witnessing a strong growth momentum this festival season, with some brands reporting a 2-3x jump in sales. Growth is driven by both premium and mass-market segments, with increased demand from tier-2 and tier-3 cities. Quick commerce and e-commerce platforms have played a significant role in boosting sales during the peak period.

articles.headline: Petronet's ₹1,200-cr biogas JV boosts domestic gas supply
articles.summary: Petronet LNG has signed a joint venture agreement with Grunner Renewable Energy to set up 10 compressed biogas (CBG) plants in India. The ₹1,200-crore project will have a combined production capacity of 180 tonnes per day. The move marks Petronet's first major foray into the domestic gas market and aims to reduce India's reliance on imported fossil fuels.

articles.headline: India's auto production set to slow in 2027
articles.summary: India's automobile industry is expected to see a slowdown in production growth in 2027, according to CIE Automotive. High inventory levels and margin pressures are cited as key reasons for the moderated outlook. While the electric vehicle segment continues to grow, traditional internal combustion engine vehicle production may see a slight decline due to shifting consumer preferences.

articles.headline: Coal costs weigh on Adani Power; tariff recovery delayed
articles.summary: Adani Power's fuel costs surged 41.8% in Q2 FY27 due to higher imported coal prices. The company noted that recovering these costs through tariff adjustments could take more than six months. Despite the cost pressure, Adani Power reported a 19% increase in power generation. The company is focusing on improving operational efficiency to mitigate the impact of high fuel prices.

articles.headline: Zee onboards Komal Nahta as Creative Director
articles.summary: Zee Entertainment Enterprises has appointed renowned film analyst Komal Nahta as Creative Director for its movies business. Nahta will be responsible for overseeing content acquisition and development across multiple languages, including Hindi and Marathi. The appointment is part of Zee's strategy to strengthen its position in the competitive media and entertainment market.

articles.headline: China's export curbs could slow India's upstream solar push
articles.summary: China's decision to restrict exports of critical solar technology components could impact India's plans to build a domestic solar manufacturing supply chain. The curbs affect technologies related to wafer and polysilicon production. Indian industry players warn this could lead to delays in setting up new manufacturing units and increase dependence on Chinese imports for now.

articles.headline: L'Oreal banks on quick commerce for India's growth
articles.summary: Global beauty giant L'Oreal is increasingly focusing on quick commerce to drive its growth in the Indian market. The company noted that products from its major brands like Garnier and Maybelline are seeing strong demand on platforms like Blinkit and Zepto. L'Oreal plans to further integrate its digital marketing strategies with these fast-delivery services to capture more consumers.

articles.headline: IFC extends $150-million loan to SBI
articles.summary: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) has provided a $150-million loan to the State Bank of India to support small businesses. The funding will particularly target women-owned enterprises and climate-friendly projects. This is part of a larger partnership between IFC and SBI to promote sustainable financial growth and entrepreneurship in India.

articles.headline: Blue Dart launches B2C cross-border delivery
articles.summary: Logistics major Blue Dart has launched a new B2C cross-border delivery service to help Indian e-commerce firms reach international customers. The service will initially cover key markets including the US, UK, and Australia. Blue Dart aims to provide a cost-effective and reliable shipping solution for small and medium-sized exporters looking to expand their global footprint.

articles.headline: AI drives productivity, but fails to spark broad growth in IT
articles.summary: While AI has improved internal productivity for Indian IT firms, it has yet to translate into significant overall revenue growth. A report by Gartner notes that companies are still in the early stages of AI adoption, with most projects focused on cost-saving rather than new business generation. High implementation costs and a lack of skilled talent remain key hurdles for the industry.

articles.headline: N. America trails Europe in revenue growth for Indian IT firms
articles.summary: For the first time in several years, Indian IT firms reported higher revenue growth in Europe compared to North America. Economic slowdown and reduced tech spending in the US have impacted large contracts. In contrast, European companies are increasing their investments in digital transformation and cloud services, providing a significant boost to Indian software exporters.

articles.headline: Pratt & Whitney signs $40 m deals with Indian firms
articles.summary: Pratt & Whitney has signed contracts worth $40 million with several Indian aerospace companies for the supply of engine components. The deals are part of the company's commitment to sourcing $500 million worth of parts from India by 2030. This move is expected to strengthen India's aerospace manufacturing ecosystem and create hundreds of high-skilled jobs.

articles.headline: Consumer, retail industry sees 127 deals worth $2b in Sept quarter
articles.summary: The consumer and retail sector in India saw 127 deals worth $2 billion in the September quarter, a 31% increase in value from the previous year. Most of the activity was driven by private equity and venture capital investments. Key segments attracting interest include e-commerce, packaged foods, and personal care. Analysts expect this trend to continue as consumer demand remains strong.

articles.headline: Lula declared winner of Brazil's presidential polls
articles.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has been declared the winner of Brazil's presidential election, narrowly defeating the incumbent Jair Bolsonaro. Lula received 50.9% of the vote in a highly polarized contest. The victory marks a significant political shift in Latin America's largest economy. Bolsonaro has not yet formally conceded, leading to some concerns about a peaceful transition of power.

articles.headline: PM Modi, BRICS leaders seek to boost cooperation
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other BRICS leaders have called for closer economic and security cooperation among member nations. During a virtual summit, the leaders discussed ways to reform global institutions and strengthen trade ties. India emphasized the need for a more inclusive international order that reflects the interests of developing countries.

articles.headline: Inflows into gold ETFs turn negative after 13 weeks
articles.summary: Investments in gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs) saw net outflows of $3.1 billion last week, ending a 13-week streak of positive inflows. The sell-off was triggered by a stronger US dollar and rising bond yields. Despite the recent drop, gold prices remain near all-time highs due to ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and uncertainty over US interest rate cuts.

articles.headline: Slack mustard coverage drags rabi acreage as sowing begins
articles.summary: Initial sowing for the rabi season in India has started on a slow note, with mustard acreage down 37% compared to last year. Farmers in Rajasthan and Haryana have delayed planting due to higher-than-normal temperatures. While wheat sowing has also begun, the overall area under cultivation is currently lower than last year, raising concerns about potential impacts on future crop yields.

articles.headline: Jan-Aug tur imports rise 44% with prices easing
articles.summary: India's imports of tur (pigeon pea) increased by 44% in the first eight months of 2026, reaching 12.58 lakh tonnes. The surge in imports has helped stabilize domestic prices, which have eased slightly in recent weeks. Most of the imports are coming from Myanmar and African countries like Mozambique and Malawi, as India looks to meet its growing domestic demand for pulses.

articles.headline: India’s crude steel output up 5.6% in Jan-Sept
articles.summary: India's crude steel production rose 5.6% year-on-year to 130 million tonnes during the first nine months of 2026. This comes at a time when global steel production has seen a slight decline. India is now the world's second-largest steel producer, supported by strong domestic demand from the infrastructure and construction sectors. However, rising raw material costs remain a concern.

articles.headline: Buyofuel, Honda Trading ink pact for biofuel supply chain
articles.summary: Buyofuel, an Indian B2B marketplace for biofuels, has signed an agreement with Honda Trading India to develop a reliable supply chain for green energy. The partnership will focus on sourcing and distributing various types of biofuels to industrial consumers. The move is part of both companies' commitment to supporting India's transition to a low-carbon economy.

articles.headline: CMFRI supplies 5 lakh mussel seeds to Maharashtra
articles.summary: The ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute has supplied 5 lakh green mussel seeds to fish farmers in Maharashtra to promote sustainable aquaculture. The initiative aims to provide alternative livelihoods for coastal communities and boost domestic mussel production. CMFRI is also providing technical training to farmers on modern mussel farming techniques.

articles.headline: Centre gives nod for ₹2.12-lakh crore defence procurement
articles.summary: The Defence Acquisition Council has approved proposals for the procurement of various weapons systems and equipment worth ₹2.12 lakh crore. The list includes indigenous multi-role helicopters, air defence systems, and anti-ship missiles. This is part of the government's efforts to modernize the armed forces and boost domestic defence manufacturing under the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' initiative.

articles.headline: Trade margin cap on cancer drugs may push up costs
articles.summary: The government's plan to cap trade margins on 137 non-scheduled cancer drugs could lead to higher prices for some patients, experts warn. While the move is aimed at reducing the maximum retail price, healthcare providers suggest that hospitals may increase other service charges to offset the loss in revenue. The health ministry is currently reviewing the proposal with stakeholders.

articles.headline: Cordelia launches its largest cruise vessel, plans expansion
articles.summary: Cordelia Cruises has launched its largest cruise vessel, the Cordelia Sky, and announced plans to add more ships to its fleet over the next three years. The company is targeting the growing domestic and international cruise market in India. Cordelia Sky will operate on various routes across India and neighboring countries, with a focus on providing a premium luxury experience.

articles.headline: The groove of freedom turns full circle with Vande Mataram vinyl
articles.summary: A special vinyl album featuring the earliest recordings of India's national song, Vande Mataram, has been released to commemorate its 121st anniversary. The album includes versions in several Indian languages and is part of a project to preserve India's musical heritage. The first copy was presented to President Droupadi Murmu at a ceremony in New Delhi.

articles.headline: RBI Approves Record Two Point Eleven Lakh Crore Dividend To Central Government
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India approved a record surplus transfer of 2.11 lakh crore rupees to the central government for the 2023-24 financial year. This amount is double the previous year's transfer and is expected to provide significant fiscal relief for government spending and deficit management.

articles.headline: Pune Doctors Arrested For Swapping Blood Samples In Porsche Accident Case
articles.summary: Pune police have arrested two doctors from Sassoon General Hospital for allegedly tampering with blood samples in the Porsche crash case involving a minor. The investigation suggests that the original blood samples were discarded and replaced with others to hide evidence of alcohol consumption during the accident.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi Claims Divine Mission In Latest Election Campaign Interview
articles.summary: In a recent interview, Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke about his sense of mission, stating that he believes his work is guided by a divine force. The comments have generated extensive discussion among various political parties as the country prepares for the remaining phases of the Lok Sabha elections.

articles.headline: Ireland Norway And Spain Formally Recognize Palestinian Statehood Amid Gaza War
articles.summary: Norway, Ireland, and Spain have officially recognized Palestine as a sovereign state, a move that will take effect on May 28. The three countries stated their decision was meant to support a two-state solution. In response, Israel recalled its ambassadors from these nations for urgent consultations.

articles.headline: Intense Heatwave Grips Northern India As Southwest Monsoon Approaches Kerala Coast
articles.summary: Severe heatwave conditions persist across northern and central India, with several cities recording temperatures above 45 degrees Celsius. Concurrently, the India Meteorological Department has forecast that the Southwest Monsoon will arrive at the Kerala coast within the coming days, offering eventual relief.

articles.headline: Rajasthan Royals Defeat RCB In Eliminator To Reach IPL Qualifier Two
articles.summary: Rajasthan Royals progressed to the second qualifier of IPL 2024 after defeating Royal Challengers Bengaluru by four wickets in the Eliminator. RR successfully chased down a target of 173 runs at the Narendra Modi Stadium. The loss ended RCB's tournament run after a series of consecutive late-season victories.

articles.headline: SEBI Bars Regulated Entities From Using Unregistered Financial Influencers For Promotion
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has introduced new rules to prevent its regulated entities from working with unregistered financial influencers. The move is intended to protect the interests of retail investors by ensuring they do not receive unverified or biased investment advice from social media.

articles.headline: Nvidia Reports Record Revenue Driven By Continued Global AI Chip Demand
articles.summary: Nvidia reported record-breaking quarterly revenue of 26 billion dollars, driven by high demand for its artificial intelligence chips. The company also announced a ten-for-one stock split and increased its dividend, signaling continued confidence in the rapid growth of the global AI industry.

articles.headline: CEC Can Only Be Removed Like Supreme Court Judge, ECI Tells Court
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India filed a joint affidavit in the Supreme Court stating that the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) cannot be removed except on grounds identical to a Supreme Court judge. The document highlights that attempts to restrain the CEC’s functioning are contrary to law and confirms that the multi-member commission follows a rule of majority for decision-making.

articles.headline: Jamia Students Refuse to End Strike Demanding Definite Election Timeline
articles.summary: Protesting students at Jamia Millia Islamia continued their hunger strike despite the university announcing that elections would be held within 15 days of a new constitution's approval. At least 20 students were detained by police for scaling campus gates. Protesters rejected the administration's verbal assurances, demanding a specific date for student union polls last held in 2006.

articles.headline: Chief Minister Inspects Trial Run of Delhi’s First Namo Yamuna Cruise Safari
articles.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta inspected the trial run of the 'Namo Yamuna Cruise Safari', scheduled for a mid-November launch. The 6-km waterway service between Sonia Vihar and Jagatpur aims to boost tourism and employment. The cruise accommodates 30 passengers for 45-minute trips. The CM emphasized that tourism development must coincide with keeping the Yamuna clean.

articles.headline: Two Bodies Recovered Following Building Collapse in Delhi’s Harsh Vihar
articles.summary: The bodies of a 60-year-old man and his son were pulled from debris after a building collapsed in north-east Delhi on Sunday. Following an overnight rescue operation by the NDRF and fire brigade, police arrested the building owner for negligence. The incident triggered a political row between AAP and BJP regarding illegal construction and the failure of municipal building audits.

articles.headline: Old Rao Tula Ram Flyover Reopens to Light Vehicles After Repairs
articles.summary: The Old Rao Tula Ram (RTR) flyover in Delhi reopened to cars and two-wheelers on Monday following repairs. Heavy motor vehicles remain barred for at least a week to allow concrete to cure. The flyover was closed on October 20 after cracks and exposed reinforcement were detected. PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh confirmed that a comprehensive structural audit of the flyover is under way.

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir Cabinet Reshuffle Set for Tuesday; Congress Stays Out
articles.summary: Five ministers in Jammu and Kashmir submitted resignations ahead of a cabinet reshuffle scheduled for Tuesday. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha will administer the oath of office to new ministers in Srinagar. Ally Congress has decided not to join the government, citing the region's continuing status as a Union Territory despite efforts by the National Conference leadership to reach out.

articles.headline: Odisha Highway Blocked to Protest Death of Youth in Police Custody
articles.summary: Residents in Malkangiri blocked National Highway 326 after 22-year-old Tanup Dey died in the custody of a visiting Haryana police team. Dey was picked up on Sunday for alleged ganja smuggling and was found hanging in a hotel room the next morning. Family members alleged police brutality and claimed the death was staged as a suicide. Local authorities are investigating the incident.

articles.headline: Mumbai Police Forms SIT to Probe ₹500 Crore Allegations Against BJP
articles.summary: A three-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed by Mumbai police to investigate claims by Maratha activist Manoj Jarange-Patil. He alleged that the BJP paid him ₹500 crore through Shrikant Shinde to "manage" the quota agitation. The probe follows the release of an audio tape by the activist. MP Sanjay Raut has also sought an Enforcement Directorate probe into the matter.

articles.headline: Ten Arrested in Madhya Pradesh After Deaths Linked to Illicit Liquor
articles.summary: Police in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh, arrested 10 people following the death of two individuals allegedly linked to spurious liquor consumption. While locals claim 13 people have died since September, the administration has only confirmed two deaths pending forensic tests. Congress leaders alleged that up to 40 people suffered vision damage and demanded a thorough investigation into the trade.

articles.headline: Junior Doctors in Kolkata Allege Threats After Flagging Mismanagement in Stampede
articles.summary: Junior doctors at Medical College Kolkata claim they are facing intimidation and threats after reporting a lack of basic facilities during the treatment of Durga Puja pandal stampede victims. The stampede killed 19 people. Health Minister Dr. Sharadwat Mukherjee dismissed the protesters as "dimagi naxals" and claimed they do not represent the majority of junior doctors in the state.

articles.headline: New FIR Filed Against Actress Urmila Sanawar in Ankita Murder Case
articles.summary: A fresh FIR was filed against television actress Urmila Sanawar in Dehradun for allegedly making defamatory remarks against BJP leaders and the family of an former MLA. Sanawar was arrested on Sunday. The complaint follows her social media posts regarding the Ankita Bhandari murder case. Congress leaders criticized the arrest, noting she had already consented to a narco-analysis test.

articles.headline: Delhi University Vice-Chancellor Says Army Should Stop Playing Sare Jahan Se Achha
articles.summary: Delhi University Vice-Chancellor Yogesh Singh argued that the Indian Army should stop playing Muhammad Iqbal’s "Sare Jahan Se Achha" in its military bands. Speaking at a book launch, Singh criticized those who sing the composition but refuse to sing "Vande Mataram." He alleged that Iqbal later advocated ideas associated with Partition, distancing himself from his earlier love for India.

articles.headline: Congress Aims to Contest 175 Seats in Uttar Pradesh Assembly Election
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam stated the party wishes to contest at least 175 of the 403 seats in the upcoming state election as part of the INDIA bloc. A list of 200 seats has been shared with ally Samajwadi Party. While SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said the focus is on removing BJP from power, some local Congress hoardings have already staked claims to specific seats.

articles.headline: Venugopal Defends Kharge’s Remark on PM as Ideological Attack Not Personal
articles.summary: Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal defended party president Mallikarjun Kharge’s comments about PM Narendra Modi’s late father, calling it an "ideological attack" on the RSS. Speaking in Chandigarh, Venugopal announced that Rahul Gandhi will lead a rally in Punjab on November 4 to launch the party's 2027 election campaign and criticized the current AAP government's law and order.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses Petition Probing Alleged Horse-Trading in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: The Supreme Court rejected a petition seeking a CBI probe into allegations of "horse-trading" involving TVK Minister Anand and four former AIADMK MLAs. The petitioner alleged the MLAs shifted allegiance to secure a majority for the ruling party. The court declined to invoke extraordinary powers to frame rules preventing resigned MLAs from contesting subsequent bypolls in the same seats.

articles.headline: Kerala High Court Stays FIR Against Pinarayi Vijayan in CMRL Case
articles.summary: ADivision Bench of the Kerala High Court stayed the FIR and investigation in the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case involving Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and family members. The court admitted appeals against a Single Bench order that directed the registration of an FIR based on an ED letter. Defense lawyers argued that the original complaint did not follow proper legal procedures under BNSS.

articles.headline: Kochi Judge Booked for Fatality After Minor Son Allegedly Rams Car
articles.summary: The Kochi City police have booked an additional district judge under the Motor Vehicles Act after his 17-year-old son allegedly killed a man in a car crash. The juvenile was granted bail, but the victim's family staged a sit-in at the police station demanding the arrest of the father-son duo. The judge is held responsible under Section 199A as the guardian and vehicle owner.

articles.headline: Malayali Diaspora in Saudi Arabia Seeks Affordable Chartered Flight Services
articles.summary: Expatriates in Saudi Arabia have requested the Kerala government to arrange chartered flights at affordable rates due to escalating conflict in the Gulf. The proposal was submitted via NoRKA-Roots following a meeting to discuss challenges faced by the diaspora. The move aims to provide relief to Malayalis struggling with high airfares and travel uncertainty in the volatile region.

articles.headline: Maharashtra Agrees to Review Telangana’s Request for Higher Tummidihatti Barrage
articles.summary: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis agreed to study Telangana's request to increase the Tummidihatti barrage height from 148 to 152 metres. A joint committee of irrigation secretaries will assess technical feasibility and impact on local land. Telangana argued the change would maximize gravity-based water conveyance. The state also pledged to compensate affected Maharashtra farmers.

articles.headline: Karnataka to Publish Final Electoral Roll After Revision Drive Deletes Millions
articles.summary: Karnataka will publish its final electoral roll on Tuesday after a clean-up drive that saw 1.07 crore names deleted. The Special Intensive Revision identified deceased voters, duplicates, and over 80 lakh individuals who had shifted residences. The state's total voter count was 5.54 crore before the revision, and the final list will be accessible on the Chief Electoral Officer's website.

articles.headline: Kerala Government Defends Move to Generic SMA Drug Citing Cost
articles.summary: The Kerala government defended switching to a generic drug for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) patients, which costs ₹15,000 compared to ₹6.5 lakh for the branded version. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan stated the generic drug from Natco Pharma has all statutory clearances and that the government eventually aims to provide SMA medicines free of cost to all patients in the state.

articles.headline: MP Congress Leader Criticizes BJP Over Imprisonment of Tribal Rights Activist
articles.summary: Madhya Pradesh Congress president Jitu Patwari condemned the arrest of activist Divya Ahirwar, who has been in jail for a month. Ahirwar was arrested while protesting for tribal rehabilitation and compensation for the Majhgaon dam project. Patwari alleged that the BJP government is using police power to silence those protecting tribal access to water, forests, and land.

articles.headline: Speaker Om Birla Says Parliaments Have Vital Duty to Listen to Youth
articles.summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla told the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi that Parliaments must understand and address the aspirations of the youth. He emphasized that empowering young people through education and technology is an investment in a nation's destiny. The forum, attended by members from Brazil, Russia, China, and others, aims to serve as a bridge for international trust.

articles.headline: The Hindu Group Launches Cancer 360 Book for Comprehensive Care Insights
articles.summary: The Hindu Group and the Cancer Institute (WIA), Adyar, launched 'Cancer 360: Overview of Detection, Treatment, Palliation'. The book provides a comprehensive view of cancer care, from early detection to palliative support. N. Ram emphasized making advanced care accessible, while oncology experts contributed chapters on multi-disciplinary treatment and patient support services.

articles.headline: Trial Judge in Lakhimpur Kheri Case Transferred Supreme Court Informed
articles.summary: The Supreme Court was informed that the judge presiding over the Lakhimpur Kheri killings case, involving Ashish Mishra, has been transferred in a routine move. The court allowed Mishra to visit his hometown for Deepavali. The case stems from the 2021 incident where eight people were killed during a farmers' protest. Victims had raised concerns about potential delays due to the transfer.

articles.headline: Bengal BJP Leaders Soften Stand Towards NDA Ally NCPI Ahead of Polls
articles.summary: West Bengal BJP leaders, including CM Suvendu Adhikari, have shown a change in stance toward the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI). Adhikari visited NCPI leader Sudip Bandyopadhyay, sparking rumors of a strategic alliance for municipal polls. While some old-timers express concern, the NCPI claims to be the second-largest NDA constituent at the Centre after the BJP.

articles.headline: Uncertainty Over Deleted Voters in Kolkata Ahead of Local Body Elections
articles.summary: With Kolkata municipal polls approaching, thousands of voters deleted during recent list revisions remain uncertain of their status. Opposition parties have urged the State Election Commissioner to include all appellants whose cases are pending in tribunals. Nearly 60 lakh names were removed statewide under the 'Absent/Shifted/Duplicate' categories, leading to widespread protests.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Assures Deleted Voters Won’t Be Prosecuted for New Registration
articles.summary: The Supreme Court orally assured that voters deleted during Maharashtra's electoral revision will not face prosecution for applying as new voters via Form 6. Thousands were marked absent due to urban redevelopment projects in Mumbai and Pune. The court agreed to hear a plea challenging the deletions and noted the need to ensure residents are not disenfranchised by relocation.

articles.headline: Kharge Accuses Government of Vote Theft During Festive Season Inflation
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged the government is preoccupied with "stealing votes" while citizens battle high inflation. He called for the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, claiming the Election Commission is acting on instructions from the PM. Kharge urged the public to join the 'Chalo Dilli' rally on November 1 to protest the mass deletion of names from electoral rolls.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Orders ₹6 Lakh Reparation for Wrongfully Incarcerated Man
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Uttar Pradesh government to pay ₹6 lakh to a man who spent six years in custody as an undertrial due to a "slipshod investigation." The court criticized the Agra police for a failure that led to the man's long incarceration before his eventual acquittal. It also ordered that the judgment be used to educate police officers in investigation processes.

articles.headline: Security Forces Raid Kuki-Zo Insurgent Camp in Manipur; 17 Arrested
articles.summary: Manipur police and CRPF raided the Sinai insurgent camp in Kangpokpi, arresting 17 people for allegedly impersonating registered cadres. The camp is one of two sites the Union Home Ministry wants relocated under a 2025 agreement. The raid follows recent ethnic violence in the state. The camp is currently in the custody of the CRPF as authorities enforce new terms for insurgent groups.

articles.headline: Five Shot Dead Inside Hotel in Guwahati; Suspect Detained
articles.summary: Five people, including the property owner and her son, were killed in a firing incident at a hotel in Guwahati’s Ulubari area on Monday night. One suspect has been detained by police. The motive for the shooting is currently unknown. One survivor is undergoing treatment in stable condition. Authorities are continuing searches for other perpetrators involved in the deadly attack.

articles.headline: Three People Paraded Naked in South Kolkata Over Minor Girl Row
articles.summary: An 18-year-old boy, his father, and a friend were paraded naked in Kolkata by family members of a 13-year-old girl. The girl’s parents and uncle were arrested for the assault and public humiliation, which was reportedly triggered by the boy visiting the minor. The victims were allegedly threatened with a gun during the 50-metre walk. Police are searching for more suspects involved.

articles.headline: Plant-Based Meat Beats Traditional Meat on Protein Bioavailability Study Finds
articles.summary: A study by CSIR-IHBT and GFI India found that plant-derived nuggets and kebabs can offer higher protein bioavailability than their chicken counterparts. Using simulated human digestion protocols, researchers observed that plant-based alternatives released more usable protein during the intestinal phase. The findings suggest these products are nutritively comparable to traditional meat.

articles.headline: RTI Data Reveals Many IITs Lack Recommended Mental Health Counsellors
articles.summary: RTI data showed that multiple IITs have mental health counsellor numbers significantly below the UGC's recommended 1:500 ratio. IIT-Kharagpur has one counsellor for every 1,136 students, while IIT-Patna has two for 4,000. The data highlights a critical shortage amid rising student suicides, with IIT-Kharagpur recording 10 deaths in five years. Most IITs also fall short of faculty reservation quotas.

articles.headline: Four Charred to Death as Car Catches Fire in Madhya Pradesh
articles.summary: Four men were killed and one injured in Madhya Pradesh’s Dhar district after their car fell into a culvert and caught fire. The accident happened late Sunday after a tyre burst while the group was returning from a temple. One passenger was thrown from the vehicle and survived, but the others were trapped and died. Police confirmed the deceased were all young men from the Sagore area.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Refuses to Relax Bail Terms for Delhi Riots Accused
articles.summary: The Supreme Court declined to relax bail conditions for Shadab Ahmad, an accused in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case. Ahmad had requested to leave Delhi to attend law classes in Ghaziabad. The court maintained that the condition requiring him to stay in the national capital must remain, warning that any misuse of liberty would lead to the immediate cancellation of his bail.

articles.headline: Tata Communications Plans ₹4,350 Crore AI-Ready Network Expansion in India
articles.summary: Tata Communications will invest ₹4,350 crore to build 10,000 km of AI-ready connectivity infrastructure. The project will link major data centre hubs in Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, and Chennai to international cable stations. Funded through operating cash flows, the expansion aims to meet rising global demand for high-capacity digital networks for AI workloads between FY 2030 and 2036.

articles.headline: Anthropic Files for US IPO After Skyrocketing Revenue Growth Disclosure
articles.summary: AI startup Anthropic, creator of Claude, has filed for an IPO on the Nasdaq. Disclosure shows H1 2026 revenue jumped 14-fold to $16.3 billion compared to the previous year. While the company faces high costs for advanced AI development, enterprise spending has grown significantly. The filing follows a confidential submission and intends to list Class A common stock under the ticker 'ANT'.

articles.headline: Hyundai Introduces Compact SUV Bayon Starting at ₹10 Lakh in India
articles.summary: Hyundai Motor India launched its new compact mid-size SUV, the Bayon, with prices starting at ₹9,99,900. The top-end model is priced at ₹18 lakh. Designed for modern customers, the vehicle features future-ready connectivity, advanced safety systems, and versatile performance. The launch aims to strengthen Hyundai's presence in the competitive Indian compact SUV market.

articles.headline: Sensex and Nifty End 0.7% Higher Recovering From Early Trade Losses
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty recovered from a 0.8% early dip to settle 0.7% higher on Monday. The Sensex gained 481 points to end at 73,606.75, while the Nifty 50 closed at 22,753.20. The recovery followed initial caution regarding West Asia tensions and central bank policies. Both indices sharply trimmed losses during the session as investor sentiment stabilized.

articles.headline: BPCL Eyes Middle East Crude as Russian Oil Discounts Fade
articles.summary: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) increased its Middle Eastern crude imports as Russian oil lost its price advantage due to rising freight costs and narrower discounts. Russian oil accounted for 37% of BPCL’s procurement in Q2, but the shift to spot crude from other regions is becoming more pronounced. BPCL officials noted that the trend would likely continue through November.

articles.headline: Jordan Arrests Three in Raid Over Deadly Church Attack
articles.summary: Jordanian security forces arrested three Islamic extremist suspects following a dawn raid and shootout linked to a church attack that killed nine people. The suspects, including two brothers, were wounded during the operation. The Director of Public Security confirmed the arrests were part of a broader crackdown following a recent surge in extremist violence in the kingdom.

articles.headline: Five Palestinians Including Child Killed in Israeli Strikes in Gaza
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip killed five Palestinians, including a young girl, on Monday. Civil defence officials reported 13 total deaths and 60 wounded over the past 24 hours. The ongoing conflict continues to result in civilian casualties as military operations intensify across the territory, leading to severe humanitarian concerns and medical shortages for residents.

articles.headline: Marine Le Pen Kicks Off Presidential Bid Vowing Restoration of Order
articles.summary: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen launched her presidential campaign with a promise to restore the "rule of law" and preserve France's cultural identity. Addressing supporters in Orleans, she criticized recent arson and looting linked to cost-of-living protests. Le Pen's bid focuses on security and national sovereignty ahead of the upcoming national elections next year.

articles.headline: Mass Power Outages in Sudan After Paramilitary Drone Attacks on Stations
articles.summary: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces (RSF) launched coordinated drone attacks against five power stations, causing massive outages in the country's eastern states. The drones hit facilities in Al-Jazira, Gedaref, and White Nile, which are under the control of the Sudanese Army. The attack marks a escalation in the ongoing conflict, directly targeting critical civilian infrastructure.

articles.headline: Kremlin Says Ukraine Offensive Will Continue Despite Local Humanitarian Truces
articles.summary: Russia announced it will not slow its offensive in Ukraine despite upcoming US-brokered talks. However, the Kremlin agreed to a local humanitarian ceasefire in the occupied city of Oleshky for medical and food supplies. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that combat operations against Ukraine's military-industrial complex would continue alongside any specific humanitarian truces.

articles.headline: India Looks to Seal T20 Series Against New Zealand in Wellington
articles.summary: India aims to clinch the T20 International series against New Zealand in the third match at Basin Reserve. The team faces challenges from gusty winds and chilly conditions. India’s unbeaten run in T20Is in New Zealand dates back to 2020. The host will miss key pacers Lockie Ferguson and Matt Henry due to workload management, giving the Indian batting order a potential advantage.

articles.headline: Devdutt Padikkal Scores 199 as India-A Recovers Against New Zealand-A
articles.summary: Devdutt Padikkal missed a double century by one run but guided India-A to a strong recovery in the first unofficial Test against New Zealand-A. India-A posted 488 for eight in their second innings, building a 288-run lead after conceding a large first-innings deficit. Padikkal shared a 210-run stand with Sai Sudharsan (91). India-A now looks for a win on the final day in Lincoln.

articles.headline: Manvir Singh Late Strike Helps Mohun Bagan Edge Chennaiyin FC 1-0
articles.summary: Manvir Singh scored an 85th-minute winner to help Mohun Bagan Super Giant defeat Chennaiyin FC in the ISL. The match at Salt Lake Stadium saw Chennaiyin dominate for long periods, with Nikola Stojanovic hitting the crossbar. However, a precise cross from Liston Colaco allowed Manvir to seal the victory. Bagan’s win was aided by critical saves from goalkeeper Vishal Kaith.

articles.headline: Ayush Badoni’s Sixth First Class Century Steers Delhi Against Jharkhand
articles.summary: Ayush Badoni scored a chanceless unbeaten 106 to lead Delhi to 309 for five on day one of their Ranji Trophy match against Jharkhand. Badoni shared a 128-run unbroken partnership with Sumit Mathur (50) to rescue Delhi from 181 for five. Badoni reached his three-figure milestone in just 111 deliveries, demonstrating his dominance over the Jharkhand spin attack in Ranchi.

articles.headline: BPCL Edges Malaysia Junior Hockey Team 1-0 in Murugappa Gold Cup
articles.summary: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) defeated the Malaysia junior team 1-0 in a Pool-B match of the Murugappa Gold Cup. Sudeep Chirmako scored the only goal in the third minute. Malaysia, fresh from winning the Sultan of Johor Cup, appeared travel-weary. BPCL dominated the game but missed several chances, including a penalty stroke, before securing their third consecutive win.

articles.headline: Team MRF Tyres Wins Fourth FIA European Rally Championship Teams Title
articles.summary: Team MRF Tyres was crowned the 2026 FIA European Rally Championship Teams’ champion after a dominant campaign. The team finished with 233 points, securing a 98-point lead over their closest rivals. Martins Sesks delivered the overall victory in the final round in Portugal. This marks MRF’s fourth title in five years, featuring a successful international line-up of drivers.

articles.headline: Kylian Mbappe Brace Condemns Barcelona to First LaLiga Defeat of Season
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe scored twice to lead Real Madrid to a 2-1 Clasico victory over league leaders Barcelona at Camp Nou. Mbappe’s goals cut Barcelona’s lead to three points. Despite a quiet first half, Raphinha leveled the score for the hosts in the 61st minute before Mbappe’s late strike secured the win for Real. The result marks Barcelona’s first domestic defeat of the campaign.

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli Wins US Grand Prix to Stand on Brink of F1 Title
articles.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli won the US GP in Austin, leaving him on the verge of becoming Formula One's youngest champion. Starting from pole, the 20-year-old Italian dominated the race, finishing ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen. Antonelli needs just two points in the upcoming Mexico City race to mathematically secure the world championship.

articles.headline: Jalandhar Prepares to Host Its First Ever International Hockey Tournament
articles.summary: Jalandhar will host its maiden international hockey event as the Asian Champions Trophy starts on Tuesday. Five members of the Indian squad learned to play at the host venue, Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium. India opens its campaign as favorites against Bangladesh. The tournament will be played on a new green turf compliant with FIH standards, marking a major milestone for the city.

articles.headline: Mohammed Shami Defends Fitness and Expresses Desire for India Team Return
