articles.summary: In an exclusive interview, veteran pacer Mohammed Shami dismissed concerns about his fitness and ability to bowl long spells. Shami, who hasn't played for India since early 2025, stated he is currently at his peak and is using domestic cricket for Bengal to stay in rhythm for a potential recall. He emphasized his loyalty to his state team and his goal of playing for India again.

articles.headline: Study Traces Kashmir Rice to East Asia Via Ancient Silk Road Routes
articles.summary: Research from SKUAST-Kashmir found that Kashmir’s traditional rice varieties are genetically linked to those in Korea and Northeast China. These varieties carry unique cold-tolerance genes, like HAN1 and CTB4a, that modern varieties have lost. The study suggests these landraces are a reservoir of resilient genes and arrived in the valley via early Silk Road trade routes thousands of years ago.

articles.headline: AI Companies Consult Faith Leaders to Build Moral Models Experts Warn
articles.summary: Major AI firms like Anthropic and Google are increasingly seeking input from philosophers and religious leaders to inform their ethical models. While some praise the intellectual curiosity, other experts warn that extracting general moral principles from religion ignores the complex, conflicting realities of diverse faiths and risks prioritizing certain world-views over others.

articles.headline: Rate hike outlook and funding costs put Indian banks on guard
articles.summary: Indian banks are preparing for potential interest rate increases and rising funding costs, with SBI Chairman C S Setty suggesting rates could rise 50 basis points by December. Tighter liquidity and changing household savings patterns are challenging deposit mobilization. Lenders at the BFSI Insight Summit noted that higher rates might moderate demand in sensitive borrowing sectors.

articles.headline: Election Commission tells SC it did not change statutory Form 6
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India clarified to the Supreme Court that it did not approval modifications to Form 6 for voter enrollment. Instead, it introduced a separate declaration form during the Special Intensive Revision to help establish applicant eligibility. The poll panel defended its collective decision-making process against allegations of unilateral action by the chief commissioner.

articles.headline: Aditya Birla Real Estate reports Rs 859 crore Q2 profit
articles.summary: Aditya Birla Real Estate reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 859 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27. This performance marks a significant turnaround compared to a loss in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. The company's stock rose 3.2% following the announcement of the quarterly results.

articles.headline: APL Apollo Tubes net profit rises 27 per cent to Rs 382 crore
articles.summary: APL Apollo Tubes reported a 27% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 382 crore for the second quarter of FY27. The company's performance reflects steady demand in the structural steel tubes segment. Following the results, the company's shares closed 2.3% higher on the stock exchange.

articles.headline: Eris Lifesciences net profit jumps 53 per cent in Q2 FY27
articles.summary: Eris Lifesciences posted a 53% year-on-year increase in net profit, reaching Rs 184 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The significant growth in earnings was supported by strong performance in its core pharmaceutical portfolio. The company's stock saw a marginal gain of 0.7% after the announcement.

articles.headline: Landmark Cars receives letter of intent for new car dealerships
articles.summary: Landmark Cars has received a letter of intent from a major manufacturer to open new dealerships. The company’s stock rose 1.5% following the announcement. This expansion is part of the firm's broader strategy to increase its retail footprint in the premium automotive segment in India.

articles.headline: Jakson Solar plans $525 million investment in solar manufacturing plants
articles.summary: Jakson Solar is investing $525.2 million to establish 3 gigawatts each of solar cell and ingot-wafer manufacturing capacity by December 2027. The move aims to build a domestic manufacturing ecosystem to avoid supply shocks and comply with upcoming local-content requirements. The facilities will primarily cater to the merchant market, reducing import dependence on China.

articles.headline: Hyundai eyes 250,000 mid-size SUV sales in India by 2027
articles.summary: Hyundai Motor India expects to sell at least 250,000 mid-size SUVs in 2027, driven by the Creta and the newly launched Bayon. The company aims to sell 170,000 Creta units in 2026 alone. Hyundai is targeting different buyer segments with the two models and plans to begin exports of the Bayon to over 50 global markets within months of its domestic launch.

articles.headline: ITC Hotels net profit rises 52 per cent to Rs 203 crore
articles.summary: ITC Hotels Limited reported a 52% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 203 crore for Q2 FY27. Revenue from operations grew 26% to Rs 1,054 crore. The company is expanding its portfolio with new properties in Puri, Visakhapatnam, and New Delhi, and has approved the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai.

articles.headline: Bonfiglioli to review royalty arrangement with Indian unit after IPO
articles.summary: Italian industrial major Bonfiglioli Group will review its 6% royalty arrangement with its Indian arm where appropriate, following the unit's recent Rs 2,534 crore IPO. Executive President Sonia Bonfiglioli stated the listing reflects the maturity of the Indian business. The group views India as a critical manufacturing and engineering hub for industrial and renewable energy applications.

articles.headline: Indian AI startups weigh costs of moving to the United States
articles.summary: Indian AI startups seeking US venture capital face challenges including high local hiring costs and visa hurdles. While VCs like Antler India and All In Capital have launched programs to help these firms enter the US, winning initial American clients remains difficult without a proven track record. Nearly half of the startups in select programs have already flipped their headquarters to the US.

articles.headline: IIT-Kharagpur to establish India’s first dedicated Physical AI school
articles.summary: IIT-Kharagpur is setting up the Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI with an investment of Rs 35 crore. The initiative, supported by philanthropist Vinod Gupta, aims to create a dedicated academic center for Physical Artificial Intelligence. Funding includes Rs 12.5 crore from the Gupta family and Rs 10 crore from an anonymous alumnus, with the institute covering the remainder.

articles.headline: Cadence unveils AI models with Nvidia to speed up chip design
articles.summary: Cadence Design Systems has launched 'Cadence Maestro', a portfolio of AI models tuned to assist human engineers in designing computer chips. Built on Nvidia’s Nemotron model and secured with Open-Shell technology, the suite aims to precisely meet cost and performance targets. The launch deepens the partnership between Cadence and Nvidia in the race for AI-driven hardware development.

articles.headline: Account Aggregator pricing model rollout deferred to December 1
articles.summary: Industry alliance Sahamati has postponed the rollout of a new pricing model for India’s Account Aggregator (AA) network to December 1, 2026. The deferral follows requests for more time during the festival season. The new model will establish a standard fee for data access through the network, replacing individual deals between financial information users and providers.

articles.headline: Three key industries fare poorly in new core sector series
articles.summary: While India's overall core sector output grew 7.9% in September, key segments including crude oil, natural gas, and fertilisers struggled. Crude oil production remained below the 2022-23 base year level for all six months of H1 FY27. None of these three segments surpassed their year-ago performance in any month of the current financial year, according to Datanomics analysis.

articles.headline: Election Commission suspends six officers over UP repoll lapses
articles.summary: The Election Commission ordered the immediate suspension of six officers for failing to ensure proper control during a repoll for the Teachers’ Constituency of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council. The repoll in Agra Division followed complaints of irregularities during initial voting. The officers were found at fault for lapses in supervision at two specific polling stations.

articles.headline: China says it is strictly abiding by border agreements with India
articles.summary: China’s Foreign Ministry stated that it is strictly following relevant agreements and common understandings regarding the Line of Actual Control. The statement emphasized that Chinese forces conduct normal border patrols to safeguard territorial sovereignty. This follows an Indian statement describing the border situation as 'disturbed from time to time.'

articles.headline: SC directs states to fund bar rooms for women advocates
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered all states and Union Territories to allocate funds for bar rooms, washrooms, and other basic amenities for women advocates in district and taluk courts. A bench led by CJI Surya Kant stated that these facilities must be provided regardless of the number of women practicing, calling the lack of such amenities a failure of the duty to ensure professional safety.

articles.headline: SpaceX bags $40 billion via debt for AI chip expenditure
articles.summary: Elon Musk announced that SpaceX has closed $40 billion in debt financing to purchase graphics processing units (GPUs) for AI computing. Musk linked the funding success to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from Starlink. For the fourth quarter, SpaceX expects up to $40 billion in capital expenditure as it builds out its AI infrastructure to support various tech operations.

articles.headline: Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise for AI infrastructure
articles.summary: Meta plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising to finance aggressive AI expansion and data center construction. The Facebook parent company has committed to spending about $825 billion on AI-related infrastructure in the future. The latest fundraising underscores a shift among big tech firms to tap equity markets for bolstering computing power.

articles.headline: SK Hynix plans $12 billion dividend from Kioxia stake gains
articles.summary: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix plans to return about 80% of its gains from selling a stake in Japan’s Kioxia Holdings to shareholders through a $12 billion special dividend. The payout is expected to be announced alongside third-quarter earnings on October 28. The company is estimated to have generated 20 trillion won in gains from the sale during the first half of the year.

articles.headline: Agnipath policy faces critical test as first batch completes training
articles.summary: The Agnipath military recruitment policy is under scrutiny as the first batch of 46,000 cadets nears the end of its four-year tenure. Only 25% will be retained as regular soldiers, while 34,500 must seek re-employment in paramilitary or civilian roles. Concerns persist regarding the long-term impact on military team spirit and the efficacy of short-term training for technical roles.

articles.headline: Universal banking is the goal for small finance bank CEOs
articles.summary: Heads of Suryoday and Equitas small finance banks (SFBs) stated at the BFSI Summit that transitioning to universal banking is a natural maturity model. They highlighted that while SFBs have expanded financial inclusion, the tag 'small finance' can lead to perceptions of higher risk. The CEOs estimated unmet credit demand among informal borrowers at Rs 85 trillion.

articles.headline: Indian banking sector has growth potential despite liquidity challenges: Axis CEO
articles.summary: Axis Bank MD Amitabh Chaudhry highlighted that while interest rate hikes are needed to combat inflation, the Indian banking system is better capitalized and more resilient than in previous cycles. He emphasized the need to strengthen deposit franchises and attract premium customers. Chaudhry also noted that working-capital cycles have lengthened due to global supply disruptions and rupee movement.

articles.headline: MFIN to issue PAN and CKYC guidelines for microfinance lenders
articles.summary: Microfinance industry body MFIN will issue guidelines within 15 days for lenders to identify borrowers using PAN and Central KYC records. The move aims to strengthen underwriting by identifying exposures across microfinance and retail loans. MFIN targets a transition period of 1.5 years to improve collection standards and address weaknesses exposed during recent periods of sector stress.

articles.headline: India must prepare for $170 billion FCNR(B) repayments: Uday Kotak
articles.summary: Veteran banker Uday Kotak warned that India faces a repayment obligation of $160-170 billion over the next three to five years as FCNR(B) deposits mature. While the inflows bought time and stabilized the rupee, he urged policymakers to prepare for eventual outflows. Kotak also called for narrower tax gaps between interest income and capital gains to support domestic savers.

articles.headline: Larger NBFCs stronger than in 2019 despite rising household leverage
articles.summary: Elaine Koh of Fitch Ratings noted that large Indian NBFCs have significantly improved their risk profiles since the 2019 crisis by shifting toward granular, secured financing. However, rapid credit growth and rising household leverage require close monitoring. Koh identified gold lending as a low-risk area but cautioned against rising speculative borrowing to invest in the metal.

articles.headline: Public sector bank chiefs say FCNR(B) was a strategic move
articles.summary: PSB heads at the BFSI summit described the record $127 billion mobilization under the FCNR(B) scheme as a strategic response to global capital flows. The scheme offered high-value depositors leverage up to nine times, multiplying funds. Leaders from SBI, PNB, and Bank of Baroda noted the inflows arrived before the busy credit season, providing funding cost relief and price stability.

articles.headline: Indian banks urged to implement Artificial Intelligence at scale
articles.summary: Private bankers at the BFSI Summit emphasized moving AI from experimentation to full-scale execution with clear business objectives. R Subramaniakumar of RBL Bank noted that RBI requires practical implementation. Bankers highlighted that AI can reimagine customer journeys and improve productivity, but warned that lenders must invest in cybersecurity and safeguards to ensure accountability.

articles.headline: Global cues to drive return of foreign capital to India
articles.summary: Foreign bankers believe India’s long-term investment prospects remain strong despite recent portfolio outflows. Capital return will depend on stabilizing interest-rate differentials and relative valuations. Standard Chartered’s P D Singh suggested outflows might have already stabilized, while HSBC’s Hitendra Dave highlighted the need for $200 billion in annual gross FDI to meet 2047 goals.

articles.headline: Funding diversification is significantly harder for smaller NBFCs
articles.summary: Smaller NBFCs face greater funding limits due to lower credit ratings compared to larger peers, according to industry leaders. Jairam Sridharan of Piramal Finance noted that access to certain markets is capped for those rated A and below. While gold loans offer a good entry point for new customers in rural areas, smaller players must pay higher costs to access domestic and international debt.

articles.headline: Economists divided over India's reliance on foreign financial capital
articles.summary: Economists at the BFSI summit debated whether India should reduce its dependence on foreign funds. Aastha Gudwani of Barclays argued foreign capital is essential for the 2047 goal and currency stability. Conversely, Samiran Chakraborty of Citibank and Sonal Varma of Nomura advocated for reducing dependence amid global volatility, noting that India needs $600 billion in foreign sources over a decade.

articles.headline: Treasury heads see prolonged strain on rupee and bond markets
articles.summary: Bank treasury heads warned that elevated crude oil prices and AI-driven foreign outflows will keep the rupee and bond markets under pressure. Shailendra Jhingan of ICICI Bank noted that FCNR(B) inflows only bought time and did not change fundamental outlooks. Treasury heads were divided on the 10-year bond yield, with some predicting it could move toward 7.8% if current conditions persist.

articles.headline: Expert advice on spotting multibagger stocks and wealth creation
articles.summary: Investment experts at the Smart Investor Arena emphasized that identifying multibaggers requires research, patience, and contrarian thinking. U R Bhat noted that earnings growth and capacity expansion are key drivers. Financial educator Anant Ladha urged young investors to focus on building active income, calling the first Rs 1 crore the hardest to earn, while EMI is the enemy of freedom.

articles.headline: Tokenisation offers shared digital ledger for real-world assets
articles.summary: Tokenisation, the recording of real-world assets like gold and real estate on a shared digital ledger, promises to make investments more liquid and accessible. Mudrex CEO Edul Patel noted that while regulatory pathways are evolving, tokenisation allows investors to divide wealth across non-correlated asset classes. Trust in these assets will depend on the regulatory umbrella provided in India.

articles.headline: Founder CEOs need to pay more attention to leadership succession
articles.summary: Joydeep Sengupta of McKinsey & Company highlighted that two-thirds of founder-CEOs in Asia do not manage leadership succession well. Speaking on the technological shift driven by AI, he said successful owner-CEOs must be comfortable with uncertainty and make quick decisions. He noted that managing talent is the single biggest issue for founders attempting to build decadal institutions.

articles.headline: Cancer drug margin caps may not lower medical bills
articles.summary: The Centre's decision to cap trade margins at 30% for 137 anti-cancer drugs may offer limited benefits to patients already enrolled in manufacturer-funded assistance programs (PAPs). Experts worry that excluding PAP volumes understates trade margins and dilutes the intended price reductions. Hospitals might also offset lost margins through higher chemotherapy or admission charges.

articles.headline: Registrar General directs states not to release provisional Census data
articles.summary: The Registrar General of India has instructed state units not to release any data or population figures from the 2027 Census to the press. RGI Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan emphasized that information collected during Census operations is strictly confidential under the Census Act of 1948. The directive aims to protect the integrity and privacy of the national accounting process.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets rebound after four-day slump
articles.summary: The BSE Sensex jumped 483 points while the Nifty rose to 22,753, snapping a four-session losing streak. The recovery was supported by value buying and a rally in metal, telecommunications, and healthcare shares. Adani Ports was the top gainer, rising 2.7%. However, sentiment remains cautious due to high crude oil prices and upcoming policy decisions by the Fed and the ECB.

articles.headline: Benchmark 10-year bond yield nears 7.5 per cent
articles.summary: India's benchmark 10-year government bond yield rose to 7.48%, its highest level since late 2022, driven by elevated crude oil prices and firm US Treasury yields. The rupee also remained under pressure, trading in the 94.90 to 95.26 range. Market participants expect the currency to stay weak due to sustained dollar demand from oil companies and foreign portfolio outflows.

articles.headline: Jio Platforms IPO fees fall short of record payday for bankers
articles.summary: Investment bankers handling the $3.1 billion Jio Platforms IPO will earn approximately Rs 196 crore in fees, equivalent to 0.65% of the issue size. This payout trails previous large offerings like Hyundai Motor India and Paytm. Fierce competition among bankers in India has compressed fees, with firms often accepting lower margins for the prestige of working on marquee transactions.

articles.headline: Muted asset quality outlook may weigh on Shriram Finance stock
articles.summary: Shriram Finance reported mixed Q2 FY27 results, with PAT rising 60% to Rs 3,680 crore but faces potential missed guidance on credit costs due to an erratic monsoon. High credit costs are expected to continue through the second half of the year. While analysts remain generally bullish on long-term growth, near-term concerns over Stage 2 asset stress in drought-affected regions persist.

articles.headline: Government clears Rs 2.12 trillion in military hardware proposals
articles.summary: The Ministry of Defence has granted Acceptance of Necessity for military hardware worth Rs 2.12 trillion, with 82% of procurements to be sourced domestically. Approved equipment includes high-mobility vehicles, tracked gun systems, air defence systems, and kamikaze drones. The acquisitions aim to improve situational awareness and combat capabilities for the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

articles.headline: Noel Tata Challenges Validity of Tata Sons Board Minutes and Filing
articles.summary: Noel Tata has urged Tata Sons to remove references to N. Chandrasekaran's reappointment from board records, calling a regulatory filing based on the resolution invalid. In a nine-page letter, he questioned the lack of a selection committee and raised conflict-of-interest concerns regarding director Venu Srinivasan, whose firm has business dealings with Chandrasekaran’s family members.

articles.headline: Government Amends Rules to Enable Use of E100 Ethanol Fuel
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has amended motor vehicle rules to permit the use of up to 100% ethanol (E100) in vehicles. The move paves the way for flex-fuel vehicles that can run on pure ethanol or various petrol-ethanol blends. The amendment provides a certification pathway for manufacturers to produce dedicated flex-fuel models, supporting sustainable energy goals.

articles.headline: Income Tax department nudges UAE property owners to disclose assets
articles.summary: The I-T department is selectively reaching out to Indian taxpayers owning property in the UAE to encourage disclosure under the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers – Disclosure Scheme, 2026. The one-time window, open until December 31, offers immunity from penalties and prosecution for declaring undisclosed foreign assets. Around 1,100 declarations have been filed since the scheme began in August.

articles.headline: Government may extend duty-free cotton imports through December
articles.summary: The Central government is poised to extend duty-free cotton imports by two months to December 2026 to curb domestic prices and support textile mills. Cotton production is projected to fall by 12-18% in the current season due to drought conditions. While domestic prices remain firm above floor levels, traders argue the move could hurt farmers in drought-hit production zones.

articles.headline: Centre committed to paring fiscal deficit: Sitharaman
articles.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated the government remains committed to reducing the fiscal deficit to below 4.5% of GDP by 2025-26. Speaking at an event, she emphasized that the national debt will be limited to 50% of GDP by 2030. She noted that a dedicated group of ministers has been working since 2014 to ensure efficient supply chain management.

articles.headline: Paytm Reports Tenfold Jump in Q2 Net Profit to 225 Crore
articles.summary: Paytm operator One 97 Communications reported a 28% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to ₹2,648 crore for the July-September quarter. Net profit surged to ₹225 crore, driven by operating leverage and AI investments. The company expects payments processing margins to improve further due to the proposed 0.4% MDR framework on select UPI transactions above ₹2,000.

articles.headline: Backdoor malware attacks on Indian small firms rise 52 per cent
articles.summary: Cybersecurity firm Kaspersky reported a 52.1% year-on-year increase in backdoor malware attacks on Indian small and medium businesses during the first half of 2026. Approximately 452,000 backdoors were detected in that period. While backdoor attacks rose, exploit detections fell by 35.1% to 463,000. Backdoors allow attackers to bypass authentication and return to steal data.

articles.headline: Meta Seeks $95 Billion in Stock Offering to Fund AI Development
articles.summary: Meta is raising up to $95 billion through common and preferred stock sales to support its race in artificial intelligence. The offering includes $35 billion in direct sales and a $60 billion at-the-market program. Major chipmakers including Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom have reportedly agreed to purchase $5 billion of the common shares to support Meta's investment in AI superintelligence.

articles.headline: Ather Energy Records First Quarterly Profit Amid 63% Revenue Growth
articles.summary: Electric scooter manufacturer Ather Energy reported its first-ever quarterly net profit of ₹1.26 crore for Q2. Operating revenue rose 63% year-on-year to ₹1,464.24 crore, driven by a 42% increase in vehicle sales to 93,211 units. The turnaround comes nearly 17 months after its listing, as the company scales production to meet rising demand despite near-term input cost pressures.

articles.headline: Tata Communications to invest $450 million in 10,000 km fibre network
articles.summary: Tata Communications plans to invest up to $450 million over three to five years to build a 10,000 km fibre network in India. This AI-ready infrastructure will offer 7.2 petabytes of capacity, connecting key data centers and AI hubs. The investment will be funded through operating cash flows and aims to capture the growing demand for high-capacity hyperscale connectivity.

articles.headline: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Term as Brazil President; Bolsonaro Contests Result
articles.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has secured a record fourth term as Brazil's President, defeating the right-wing opposition. Following the result, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro refused to concede, calling for the vote to be annulled over judicial extensions of voting hours. World leaders have congratulated Lula, but the victory sparked initial market volatility amid fears of democratic instability.

articles.headline: AP and Odisha Evacuate Residents as Cyclone Arnab Nears Coast
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have stepped up evacuations as Cyclone Arnab approaches, with a likely landfall near Kakinada on Wednesday. AP issued red alerts for seven districts, and thousands of pregnant women are being moved to hospitals. Odisha has readied 1,700 shelters. The "very severe" storm is expected to bring winds up to 140 kmph and extremely heavy rainfall across the coastal belt.

articles.headline: L&T Technology Services secures five-year engineering contract with Nokia
articles.summary: L&T Technology Services (LTTS) has established a five-year contract with Nokia to support engineering and R&D activities in India. The collaboration integrates LTTS’s engineering capabilities with Nokia’s telecommunications technology. The deal covers product engineering, software development, system integration, and product support across Nokia’s research and development programs.

articles.headline: Media Association Challenges Government’s Data Privacy Law in Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) has challenged the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act in the Supreme Court, citing violations of journalistic freedom. The petition argues the law restricts the right to information and lacks distinct exemptions for news activity. It also contests the government's power to requisition information from publishers without judicial oversight.

articles.headline: Mankind Pharma Quarterly Profit Jumps 39% on Chronic Therapy Demand
articles.summary: Mankind Pharma reported a 39% rise in consolidated net profit to ₹711 crore for the September quarter. Revenue growth was driven by strong domestic demand for chronic treatments, such as diabetes and cardiovascular medications. The company continues to see steady momentum in its prescription formulations and consumer healthcare segments, including brands like Prega News.

articles.headline: Centre Approves Defence Procurement Deals Worth ₹2.12 Lakh Crore
articles.summary: The Defence Acquisition Council, chaired by Rajnath Singh, approved capital acquisition proposals worth ₹2.12 lakh crore for the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force. Approximately 82% of the deals will be sourced indigenously. Approvals include high mobility vehicles, air defence systems, naval platforms, and various unmanned aerial systems to boost combat readiness and domestic manufacturing.

articles.headline: Student-Led Movement Defeats Strongman Aleksandar Vucic in Serbia Snap Election
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia's snap election after 14 years of power. The victory went to a student-led opposition movement, "Students’ List," which won nearly 140 seats in the 250-seat Assembly. The political shift follows years of anti-government protests. Vucic blamed independent media and foreign interference for his party’s loss amid a near-record voter turnout.

articles.headline: Mecca Pact Nations Hold De-escalation Talks With Iran in Tehran
articles.summary: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian to prevent the regional war from expanding. The Mecca pact nations discussed mechanisms to stop the cycle of violence in West Asia. While no formal pact was signed, all parties agreed to continue discussions on regional security and the use of shared resources among Islamic countries.

articles.headline: Violence Marks Shutdown Against 1,605-Megawatt Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project
articles.summary: Parts of Arunachal Pradesh's Upper Subansiri faced paralysis during a 12-hour shutdown on Monday. The protest, led by the All Tagin Students’ Union, led to the cancellation of a public hearing for the 1,605-MW Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project. Protesters damaged vehicles and equipment to oppose the dam, citing concerns over environmental impact and indigenous community interests.

articles.headline: Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh Arrested in Multi-Crore Corruption Case
articles.summary: Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi was arrested by Chennai police in connection with an alleged multi-crore scam involving the collection of "party funds" from private school managements. The arrest followed the dismissal of his anticipatory bail plea by the Madras High Court. Former CM M.K. Stalin condemned the arrest, calling it an act of political vendetta to distract from governance failures.

articles.headline: SBI Chairman Expects 50 Bps Rate Hike in December Policy
articles.summary: SBI Chairman CS Setty anticipates a 50-basis point hike in the repo rate by the Reserve Bank of India in December. Setty noted that while high rates might moderate discretionary spending-related loans, system-level asset quality remains robust. He expects a pause in the rate cycle following the December increase, as the country balances growth with inflation management.

articles.headline: Britannia Fined Over Misleading Claims for 100% Whole Wheat Bread
articles.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) fined Britannia Industries ₹1 lakh for misleading advertisements. The company's "100% whole wheat bread" was found to contain only 62% wheat flour (atta). The CCPA ordered Britannia to immediately discontinue the ads across all media and submit a compliance report within 15 days, highlighting unethical retention of consumers through deception.

articles.headline: Jio BlackRock launches Advantage World Equity Fund
articles.summary: Jio BlackRock International AMC has launched the Jio BlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund, providing Indian investors access to global equity markets through a feeder-fund structure. The open-ended retail scheme requires a minimum initial investment of $5,000. It aims to complement domestic portfolios with exposure to global firms and sectors across developed markets like the US and Japan.

articles.headline: IOB Q2 net profit surges 56% on net interest income growth
articles.summary: Indian Overseas Bank reported a 56% year-on-year jump in net profit to ₹1,912 crore for the second quarter. The performance was driven by a 26% increase in net interest income and improved asset quality, with gross NPA falling to 1.19%. The bank's total business crossed ₹7.53 lakh crore, and it plans to raise $500 million through an ESG bond issue.

articles.headline: SBI considers 'YONO Bharat' app to reach 300 million more customers
articles.summary: State Bank of India is developing 'YONO Bharat', a smaller, device-neutral version of its banking app to reach customers with basic handsets. SBI Chairman C S Setty aims to bring 300 million more customers on board by 2030 through this variant. The bank is also using Gen AI for internal knowledge management and consolidating its cheque-clearing centers into a national center run by AI.

articles.headline: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank posts record quarterly profit of Rs 451 crore
articles.summary: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank (TMB) achieved its highest-ever quarterly net profit of Rs 451.14 crore in Q2 FY27, a 42% increase year-on-year. The performance was driven by higher interest income and cost control measures. The bank's Return on Assets reached a historic high of 2.18%, and it has already met 80% of its expected credit loss requirements under new norms.

articles.headline: ASUSE to track hurdles faced by Indian women entrepreneurs
articles.summary: The Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) will, for the first time, introduce questions to capture gender-specific constraints faced by female entrepreneurs. Starting in April 2027, the survey will also move to an April–March financial year cycle to align with other economic statistics. The changes aim to provide evidence for policy discussions on women's economic participation.

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court Cancels All OBC Certificates Issued In Bengal Since 2010
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court cancelled the OBC status of several communities in West Bengal, striking down thousands of certificates issued since 2010. The court found that the state government failed to provide sufficient data to justify their inclusion. The West Bengal government has expressed intentions to challenge the ruling.

articles.headline: Court Acquits Rahul Gandhi in 2018 Defamation Case Over Amit Shah Remark
articles.summary: An MP/MLA court in Sultanpur acquitted Rahul Gandhi in a defamation case concerning remarks made in 2018 where he allegedly called Amit Shah a "murder accused." The court dismissed the case after Gandhi argued the statement was taken out of context. Congress leaders hailed the verdict as a victory against political criminalization and a validation of Gandhi's fight for truth.

articles.headline: Rajnath Singh Says Kharge’s Remarks on Prime Minister Hurt Millions
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh criticized Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for remarks about PM Narendra Modi's late father, stating they hurt the sentiments of crores of Indians. Singh said political opposition should not violate personal decorum or family dignity. He called the comments a reflection of the Congress party's ideological decline and an attack on Indian political culture.
